subproblems.title: An n-covector pulled back by the orthogonal projection onto a subspace of dimension < n vanishes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be a linear subspace with dim V < n and orthogonal projection p_V = V.starProjection. Then for every n-covector β on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) the pulled-back covector β∘p_V := β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection, (β∘p_V)(u) = β(p_V u_0, …, p_V u_{n−1}), is the zero covector.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V < n → ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected proof ("For every n-covector β and every u, the n vectors p u_0, …, p u_d lie in V, whose dimension is r < n, so they are linearly dependent, and the alternating map β vanishes on them (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). Thus β∘p = 0"), stated for an arbitrary degree n.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; an n-covector is β : Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ; p := V.starProjection = V.subtypeL ∘L V.orthogonalProjectionOnto, so p x = ↑(V.orthogonalProjectionOnto x) ∈ V (Submodule.starProjection_apply); β∘p := β.compContinuousLinearMap p, with (β∘p)(u) = β(p∘u) = β(p u_0, …, p u_{n−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).
1. (Reduction to values.) Two continuous alternating maps are equal when they agree at every argument family (ext). Fix u : Fin n → ℝ^P; since the zero map takes the value 0 everywhere (ContinuousAlternatingMap.coe_zero), it suffices to prove β(p u_0, …, p u_{n−1}) = 0.
2. (The projected family is linearly dependent.) Suppose the family w := (p u_i)_{i ∈ Fin n} in ℝ^P were linearly independent. Put w'_i := V.orthogonalProjectionOnto u_i ∈ V; then w = V.subtype ∘ w' by the definition of p. If the image of a family under a linear map is linearly independent then so is the family (LinearIndependent.of_comp, applied to the linear map V.subtype); hence w' is a linearly independent family of n vectors in the finite-dimensional space V, and therefore n = card(Fin n) ≤ dim V (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, Fintype.card_fin). This contradicts the hypothesis dim V < n. Hence w is not linearly independent.
3. (Alternating forms vanish on dependent families.) β.toAlternatingMap is an alternating ℝ-multilinear map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ over the field ℝ (a domain, and ℝ is torsion-free over itself); such a map vanishes on every family that is not linearly independent (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). By step 2, β(p∘u) = β.toAlternatingMap(w) = 0.
4. (Conclusion.) As u was arbitrary, β∘p = 0 by step 1. (If n = 0 the hypothesis dim V < 0 is impossible, so the claim is vacuous; the argument above needs no case split.) ∎

theorem Submission.cbr_ci_cp_comp_starProjection_eq_zero_of_finrank_lt : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V < n → ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, β.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection = 0 := by

  apply β.toAlternatingMap.map_linearDependent
  intro hli
  have hli' : LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => V.orthogonalProjectionOnto (u i)) := by
    apply LinearIndependent.of_comp V.subtype
    exact hli
  have hcard := hli'.fintype_card_le_finrank
  rw [Fintype.card_fin] at hcard
  omega
proof_key_steps: Reduce β∘p_V = 0 to β(p_V u_0, …, p_V u_{n−1}) = 0 for every family u (ext, compContinuousLinearMap_apply).
p_V∘u = V.subtype ∘ (orthogonalProjectionOnto ∘ u) is not linearly independent: otherwise LinearIndependent.of_comp gives n linearly independent vectors in V, so n ≤ dim V < n.
An alternating form vanishes on a linearly dependent family (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent), so β(p_V∘u) = 0.

subproblems.title: An n-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P is the span of an orthonormal n-frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let V ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be a linear subspace with dim V = n. Then there is an orthonormal family v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, indexed by Fin n, with span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} = V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → ∃ v : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the selected proof ("As dim V = n, V has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed along finrank ℝ V = n); let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be its image in ℝ^P. Then v is orthonormal in ℝ^P and span{v_0, …, v_d} = V"), stated for an arbitrary dimension n.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; V carries the restricted inner product and is a finite-dimensional real inner product space; ι := V.subtype : V →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ^P is the inclusion, which is the linear isometry V.subtypeₗᵢ.
1. (An orthonormal basis of V indexed by Fin n.) A finite-dimensional real inner product space has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin (finrank): stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V : OrthonormalBasis (Fin (finrank ℝ V)) ℝ V. Reindexing it along the bijection finCongr h : Fin (finrank ℝ V) ≃ Fin n given by the hypothesis h : finrank ℝ V = n (OrthonormalBasis.reindex) yields an orthonormal basis b = (b_0, …, b_{n−1}) of V.
2. (Orthonormal in ℝ^P.) Put v_i := ι(b_i) = ↑b_i ∈ ℝ^P. A linear isometry preserves inner products, so ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = ⟨b_i, b_j⟩ = [i = j]; that is, v is orthonormal in ℝ^P (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry applied to b.orthonormal and V.subtypeₗᵢ).
3. (Span.) range v = ι(range b) (Set.range_comp), so span(range v) = map ι (span(range b)) (Submodule.span_image). The vectors of a basis span the whole space, span(range b) = ⊤ (Basis.span_eq for b.toBasis, whose underlying family is b by OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis). Hence span(range v) = map ι ⊤ = range ι = V (Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).
4. (Conclusion.) v : Fin n → ℝ^P is orthonormal and span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} = V. (For n = 0, V = 0 and v is the empty family; the argument is uniform in n.) ∎

theorem Submission.cbr_ci_cp_exists_orthonormal_frame_of_finrank_eq : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → ∃ v : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ v ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = V := by

  refine ⟨fun i => (b i : Euclid P), ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact b.orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry V.subtypeₗᵢ
  · have hrange : Set.range (fun i => (b i : Euclid P)) = (V.subtype) '' Set.range b := by
      rw [← Set.range_comp]; rfl
    have hb : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range b) = ⊤ := by
      simpa [OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis] using b.toBasis.span_eq
    rw [hrange, Submodule.span_image, hb, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype]
proof_key_steps: Reindex stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V along finrank ℝ V = n to an orthonormal basis b of V indexed by Fin n.
v_i := ↑b_i is orthonormal in ℝ^P because the inclusion V.subtypeₗᵢ is a linear isometry.
span(range v) = map V.subtype (span(range b)) = map V.subtype ⊤ = V.

subproblems.title: Negating the first vector of an orthonormal frame keeps it orthonormal with the same span and negates every covector value
subproblems.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P), indexed by Fin (d + 1). Then there is an orthonormal family w = (w_0, …, w_d) in ℝ^P with span{w_0, …, w_d} = span{v_0, …, v_d} and β(w_0, …, w_d) = −β(v_0, …, v_d) for every (d+1)-covector β on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ v → ∃ w : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ w ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) ∧ ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), β w = -β v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the selected proof ("If s = −1, let v' := (−v_0, v_1, …, v_d) (Function.update v 0 (−v_0)): v' is orthonormal, span{v'} = span{v} = V, and β(v') = −β(v) by linearity of β in its first argument (MultilinearMap.map_update_smul / map_neg on β.toAlternatingMap)").
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P; ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; Function.update f i x is f with its i-th entry replaced by x; a (d+1)-covector is β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1) = Euclid P [⋀^Fin (d + 1)]→L[ℝ] ℝ; 0 is the first index of Fin (d + 1), which exists because d + 1 ≥ 1.
1. (Signs.) Let c : Fin (d+1) → ℝ, c := Function.update (fun _ => 1) 0 (−1), i.e. c_0 = −1 and c_i = 1 for i ≠ 0; then c_i·c_i = 1 for every i. Let w := Function.update v 0 (−v_0) = (−v_0, v_1, …, v_d). Then w_i = c_i • v_i for every i: for i = 0 both sides equal −v_0, and for i ≠ 0 both sides equal v_i.
2. (w is orthonormal.) For all i, j: ⟨w_i, w_j⟩ = ⟨c_i • v_i, c_j • v_j⟩ = c_i·(c_j·⟨v_i, v_j⟩) (real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right), and ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = [i = j] because v is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite). If i = j this equals c_i·(c_i·1) = 1 by step 1; if i ≠ j it equals c_i·(c_j·0) = 0. Thus ⟨w_i, w_j⟩ = [i = j] for all i, j, i.e. w is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite).
3. (Equal spans.) Each w_i = c_i • v_i is a scalar multiple of an element of range v, hence lies in span(range v); so span(range w) ≤ span(range v) (Submodule.span_le, Submodule.smul_mem, Submodule.subset_span). Conversely, by step 1, v_i = (c_i·c_i) • v_i = c_i • (c_i • v_i) = c_i • w_i (one_smul, smul_smul) lies in span(range w); so span(range v) ≤ span(range w). By antisymmetry span{w_0, …, w_d} = span{v_0, …, v_d}.
4. (Covector values change sign.) Let β be a (d+1)-covector. Linearity of β in its 0-th argument gives β(update v 0 ((−1) • v_0)) = (−1) • β(update v 0 v_0) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_update_smul), and update v 0 v_0 = v (Function.update_eq_self). Since (−1) • x = −x (neg_one_smul), the left side is β(w) and the right side is −β(v); hence β(w) = −β(v).
5. (Conclusion.) w is orthonormal, span{w_0, …, w_d} = span{v_0, …, v_d}, and β(w) = −β(v) for every (d+1)-covector β. ∎

      exact hc i
    · simp only [hij, ↓reduceIte, mul_zero]
  · rw [← hw]
    apply le_antisymm
    · rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
      exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩)
    · rw [Submodule.span_le]
      rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
      have h : v i = c i • (c i • v i) := by
        rw [smul_smul, hc i, one_smul]
      rw [h]
      exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩)
  · intro β
    have h := β.map_update_smul v 0 (-1 : ℝ) (v 0)
    rw [neg_one_smul, Function.update_eq_self] at h
    rw [h, neg_one_smul]
proof_key_steps: Take c := update 1 0 (−1) (so c_i·c_i = 1) and w := update v 0 (−v_0), so that w_i = c_i • v_i.
⟨w_i, w_j⟩ = c_i c_j ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = [i = j], so w is orthonormal.
w_i = c_i • v_i and v_i = c_i • w_i give span(range w) = span(range v).
Linearity of β in slot 0 (map_update_smul with scalar −1, update_eq_self) gives β(w) = −β(v).

subproblems.title: α(b) = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩)·α(τ) for a family b in the span of an orthonormal frame τ (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P) and let b = (b_0, …, b_{n−1}) be a family in ℝ^P with every b_j ∈ span{τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}}. Then for every n-covector α on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n), α(b_0, …, b_{n−1}) = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩)_{i,j}·α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}), the matrix having (i, j) entry inner ℝ (τ i) (b j).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the selected proof ("Restricted to V, every n-covector γ gives an alternating n-form γ|_V on the n-dimensional space V; by uniqueness of top-degree alternating forms (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det with the basis v of V), γ|_V = γ(v)·det_v … Concretely p x = Σ_b⟨v_b, x⟩v_b and det_v(p u) = det(⟨v_b, u_a⟩)"), in the concrete determinant form of the comparator-accepted DAG theorem dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1.graph_orientation_jacobian-a1.covector_frame_det-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 73310ec921452a01670f397b34d1cf3cd7135598), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is that theorem's reviewed proof, with indices written 0-based and the notation of this decomposition.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; an n-covector of ℝ^P is α : Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (a continuous alternating n-linear map); L := span ℝ (range τ) ⊆ ℝ^P; for a family c : Fin n → L, ↑c denotes the underlying family in ℝ^P.
1. (A basis of L indexed by Fin n.) An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of its span: e := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent is a basis (e_0, …, e_{n−1}) of L whose underlying vectors are ↑e_i = τ_i (Module.Basis.span_apply).
2. (Restriction of α to L.) Let α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype, i.e. α_L(c_0, …, c_{n−1}) := α(↑c_0, …, ↑c_{n−1}) for c_i ∈ L; it is an alternating n-linear form on L. Put b'_j := ⟨b_j, hb_j⟩ ∈ L (hypothesis b_j ∈ L). Then α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α(↑e) = α_L(e) (both by unfolding, using ↑e_i = τ_i).
3. (Top-degree uniqueness.) Alternating n-forms on the n-dimensional space L with basis e are multiples of the basis determinant: α_L = α_L(e) • det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b').
4. (The coordinate matrix.) det_e(b') = det M with M_ij := e.repr(b'_j)_i (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). We claim M_ij = ⟨τ_i, b_j⟩. Indeed b'_j = Σ_l M_lj • e_l (Module.Basis.sum_repr); taking underlying vectors (Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul) gives b_j = Σ_l M_lj • τ_l, and taking the inner product with τ_i and using orthonormality, ⟨τ_i, Σ_l M_lj τ_l⟩ = M_ij (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Hence M = Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j).
5. (Conclusion.) Combining steps 2–4: α(b) = α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b') = α(τ)·det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩) = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩)·α(τ). The argument is uniform in n; for n = 0 both sides reduce to α of the empty family, the empty determinant being 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ orthonormal ⇒ linearly independent ⇒ basis e := Module.Basis.span of L = span(range τ) with ↑e_i = τ_i.
Restrict α to L: α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype; α(b) = α_L(b′) and α(τ) = α_L(e).
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e, so α(b) = α(τ)·det_e(b′).
det_e(b′) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix, whose (i, j) entry is ⟨τ_i, b_j⟩ by expanding b_j = Σ_l c_l τ_l and orthonormality.
Hence α(b) = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩)·α(τ).

subproblems.title: Fact (O1): evaluation on an orthonormal n-frame is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n) and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then |α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1})| ≤ |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → |α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact (O1), used in step 6 of the selected proof (|β₁(v)| ≤ |β₁| ≤ 1); it is consequence (O1) of Fact (O) in the proof of cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes (the parent of the selected node) ("if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α|: extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²"). This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_eval_le-a1, status accepted, candidate commit b7846b639953f647296619e6e73dec8a8a22ba73), already a declared prerequisite of the selected node, reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the self-contained proof reviewed in the decomposition of cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes (the Hilbert–Schmidt identity is proved in step 1). Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k (continuous alternating k-linear forms); for b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin k → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(k−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e∘I)²)^{1/2} (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).
1. Hilbert–Schmidt identity (Fact (O) of the cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes proof). For every k-covector α on ℝ^P and every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (a) Standard basis: if j is not injective then e∘j has two equal entries and α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating; every injective j is uniquely I∘π with I strictly increasing (the increasing enumeration of range j) and π ∈ Perm(Fin k), the map (I, π) ↦ I∘π being injective; α(e∘(I∘π)) = sign(π)·α(e∘I), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)², and summing over the k! permutations for each I gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (b) Basis invariance: put O_{ml} := ⟨e_m, f_l⟩, so f_l = Σ_m O_{ml}e_m and, by Parseval for the orthonormal basis f, Σ_l O_{ml}O_{m'l} = Σ_l ⟨e_m, f_l⟩⟨e_{m'}, f_l⟩ = ⟨e_m, e_{m'}⟩ = δ_{mm'}. By multilinearity α(f∘j) = Σ_{m : Fin k → Fin P} (Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)})·α(e∘m), hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Σ_j Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)}O_{m'(a)j(a)} = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a (Σ_l O_{m(a)l}O_{m'(a)l}) = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a δ_{m(a)m'(a)} = Σ_m α(e∘m)² (the sum over j of a product of functions of the separate coordinates j(a) is the product of the sums), which is k!·|α|_E² by (a).
2. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P, ι(k) := Fin.castLE k (injective). Define v(i) := τ(⟨i, h⟩) if h : i < n and v(i) := 0 otherwise, and s := {i : Fin P | i < n}; v restricted to s is τ composed with the bijection s ≃ Fin n, hence orthonormal, so Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ ℝ^P with f(i) = v(i) for i ∈ s; in particular f(ι(k)) = τ(k) for every k.
3. (Permuted frames.) For π ∈ Perm(Fin n), f∘(ι∘π) = (f∘ι)∘π = τ∘π and α(τ∘π) = sign(π)·α(τ) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so α(f∘(ι∘π))² = α(τ)².
4. (Comparison.) The map π ↦ ι∘π from Perm(Fin n) to Fin n → Fin P is injective and every term α(f∘j)² is ≥ 0, so n!·α(τ)² = Σ_{π} α(f∘(ι∘π))² ≤ Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² by step 1 (with k = n); here |Perm(Fin n)| = n!.
5. (Conclusion.) Dividing by n! > 0 gives α(τ)² ≤ |α|_E²; since |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E. For n = 0 the argument is the same (τ is empty, n! = 1). ∎
Formalization note: the extension lemma needs Orthonormal ℝ (s.domRestrict v); Parseval is OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner and the product-of-sums step is Fintype.prod_sum.
proof_key_steps: Hilbert–Schmidt identity: Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E² for every orthonormal basis f (standard-basis count plus orthogonal invariance).
Extend τ to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f(castLE k) = τ(k).
The n! permuted frames τ∘π contribute n!·α(τ)² ≤ Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|_E², hence |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E.

subproblems.title: Fact (O2): a unit covector attaining 1 on an orthonormal n-frame (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then there is an n-covector β on ℝ^P with |β|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 and β(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 ∧ β τ = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact (O2), used in step 4 of the selected proof (β₂ with |β₂| = 1 and β₂(v) = 1); it is consequence (O2) of Fact (O) in the proof of cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes (the parent of the selected node) ("β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩) is a k-covector with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1: in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k)"). This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_norming-a1, status accepted, candidate commit baaca6e45ef59dcdc4a449dbbfe914c226ee5d7b), already a declared prerequisite of the selected node, reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the self-contained proof reviewed in the decomposition of cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes. Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P with standard orthonormal basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k (continuous alternating k-linear forms); for b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin k → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(k−1)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e∘I)²)^{1/2} (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).
1. (Definition of β.) For u : Fin n → ℝ^P let M(u) be the n×n matrix M(u)_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, u_k⟩ and β(u) := det M(u). Column k of M(u) depends linearly on u_k and the determinant is multilinear and alternating in the columns, so β is an alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P; it is continuous because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. Hence β ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n.
2. (β(τ) = 1.) By orthonormality ⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩ = δ_{ik} (orthonormal_iff_ite), so M(τ) = 1 and β(τ) = det 1 = 1.
3. Hilbert–Schmidt identity (Fact (O) of the cbr_ci_constant_cycle_planes proof). For every k-covector α on ℝ^P and every orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (a) Standard basis: if j is not injective then e∘j has two equal entries and α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating; every injective j is uniquely I∘π with I strictly increasing (the increasing enumeration of range j) and π ∈ Perm(Fin k), the map (I, π) ↦ I∘π being injective; α(e∘(I∘π)) = sign(π)·α(e∘I), so α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)², and summing over the k! permutations for each I gives Σ_j α(e∘j)² = k!·|α|_E². (b) Basis invariance: put O_{ml} := ⟨e_m, f_l⟩, so f_l = Σ_m O_{ml}e_m and, by Parseval for the orthonormal basis f, Σ_l O_{ml}O_{m'l} = Σ_l ⟨e_m, f_l⟩⟨e_{m'}, f_l⟩ = ⟨e_m, e_{m'}⟩ = δ_{mm'}. By multilinearity α(f∘j) = Σ_{m : Fin k → Fin P} (Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)})·α(e∘m), hence Σ_j α(f∘j)² = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Σ_j Π_a O_{m(a)j(a)}O_{m'(a)j(a)} = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a (Σ_l O_{m(a)l}O_{m'(a)l}) = Σ_{m,m'} α(e∘m)α(e∘m') Π_a δ_{m(a)m'(a)} = Σ_m α(e∘m)² (the sum over j of a product of functions of the separate coordinates j(a) is the product of the sums), which is k!·|α|_E² by (a).
4. (n ≤ P and an orthonormal basis extending τ.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so n ≤ finrank ℝ ℝ^P = P. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P, ι(k) := Fin.castLE k (injective). Define v(i) := τ(⟨i, h⟩) if h : i < n and v(i) := 0 otherwise, and s := {i : Fin P | i < n}; v restricted to s is τ composed with the bijection s ≃ Fin n, hence orthonormal, so Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ ℝ^P with f(i) = v(i) for i ∈ s; in particular f(ι(k)) = τ(k) for every k.
5. (Values on basis tuples.) Fix j : Fin n → Fin P; since τ_i = f_{ι(i)}, M(f∘j)_{ik} = ⟨f_{ι(i)}, f_{j(k)}⟩ = [ι(i) = j(k)]. (a) If j = ι∘π for some π ∈ Perm(Fin n), then f∘j = τ∘π and β(f∘j) = sign(π)·β(τ) = ±1, so β(f∘j)² = 1. (b) Otherwise β(f∘j) = 0: if some j(k) ∉ range ι, column k of M(f∘j) is zero (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_column_eq_zero); if range j ⊆ range ι, then j = ι∘ρ for a map ρ : Fin n → Fin n that is not a permutation, hence not injective (Finite.injective_iff_bijective), so f∘j has two equal entries and β(f∘j) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). (c) π ↦ ι∘π is injective, so exactly n! tuples fall under (a), and Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} β(f∘j)² = n!.
6. (Norm.) By step 3 (k = n, α = β): n! = n!·|β|_E². As n! > 0, |β|_E² = 1, and as |β|_E ≥ 0, |β|_E = 1.
7. (Conclusion.) covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 (step 6) and β τ = 1 (step 2). ∎
Formalization note: β of step 1 can be built as the ContinuousAlternatingMap with underlying alternating map Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap (LinearMap.pi fun i => innerₛₗ ℝ (τ i)) (its value is det of the transpose of M(u), Matrix.det_transpose), continuity from Continuous.matrix_det / Continuous.matrixOf (fun_prop), packaged with ContinuousAlternatingMap.mk; the extension lemma needs Orthonormal ℝ (s.domRestrict v).
proof_key_steps: β(u) := det(⟨τ_i, u_k⟩) is an n-covector with β(τ) = det 1 = 1.
In an orthonormal basis f extending τ, β(f∘j) = ±1 when j = ι∘π for a permutation π and 0 otherwise, so Σ_j β(f∘j)² = n!.
The Hilbert–Schmidt identity Σ_j β(f∘j)² = n!·|β|_E² gives |β|_E = 1.
